title: Minute-zero SDK handoff protocols — sketch
summary: Working sketch for a "minute-zero" handoff that gets a new SDK consumer from signup to a reproducible, instrumented first call in under 15 minutes. Focus is pragmatic: simple commands, telemetry contract, fallbacks, and an internal checklist for SRE/SE handoffs.
audience: internal: SDK engineers, solutions engineering, docs writers, SREs, onboarding team
goals: Define a minimal reproducible first-call path for customers (hosted + local dev)
Specify the telemetry events + labels we require for early signal (latency, error-code, token-count, client-id)
Create a short handoff checklist for SEs to run when a customer hits 'first failure'
Ensure a rollback/mitigation recipe for common flakiness in first 24h
scope: Covers hosted API quickstart and the local dev shim (dockerized sample app). Does NOT cover enterprise private deployment install steps — those live in private-deployments docs. This is intentionally minimal: no deep SDK internals, focus on consumer experience and observability.
assumptions: Customer has a Redwood API key and basic network egress to our hosted endpoints
Sample app runs on macOS/Linux or in provided Docker image
Telemetry backend (events ingestion) is reachable and SE has permission to view the first-48h stream
prerequisites: Redwood API key (instructions: console > credentials > create key)
Access to the onboarding Slack channel (#onboard-sdk)
SE has read access to sandbox telemetry dashboards
quickcommands:
# quick hosted test (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"small-llm-1","input":"hello"}'

# dockerized sample start
docker run --rm -e RW_KEY=$RW_KEY ghcr.io/redwood/sdk-starter:minute-zero
hand_off_steps: Confirm customer created API key and can curl the /health endpoint
Ask customer to run the quick curl command while the SE watches telemetry (live ingestion) for their client-id tag
If request succeeds but latency is high (>500ms p50), check region routing and model tier mapping
If request fails with 4xx, verify key scoping and billing state; if 429, check rate limit headers and advise backoff policy
For local docker issues, ask for docker logs and reproduce locally following the exact command the customer used
telemetry_contract: Minimal event schema required for 'minute-zero' success signal: event_type (request_start|request_end|error), client_id (anonymized token), model_name, region, request_id, status_code, latency_ms, token_input_count, token_output_count, error_code (if present), sdk_version, platform (hosted|docker|local). Events should arrive within 10s of call in ingestion path for SE realtime debugging.
abort_and_rollback: If ingestion shows systemic 5xx for a region: switch routing to fallback region and notify infra on-call
If sample app is consistently failing due to auth: revoke and reissue a short-lived API key and test again
If customer hits rate limits during onboarding: temporarily raise soft limits for 30 minutes and schedule a follow-up quota plan
outstanding_questions: Do we want a one-click 'minute-zero' sandbox in Console that auto-populates a sample curl with the customer's key? (security implications)
Should SDKs emit a distinct 'first_call' telemetry event to make onboarding funnels visible in analytics?
What is the minimum retention for onboarding telemetry to support 72h root cause analysis?
notes_to_self: Keep this short and prescriptive. Customers get overwhelmed by multi-page guides on day one. SEs need a single checklist and a 'what I will ask you to run' script. Add links to the short video demo once recorded. Follow up: prototype a Console one-click later this quarter.
